reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only generally discusses surface modification of TC4 and laser cladding of multi-principal alloy coatings, without addressing refractory HEAs, in-situ carbide reinforcement, graded interfaces, or the specific performance improvements claimed. The key premises lack direct, specific prior support.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a refractory HEA coating on TC4 with a uniform, dense microstructure and good metallurgical bonding.
In-situ formed carbide particles (e.g., WC) can be uniformly dispersed in a laser-clad HEA coating to act as dispersion-strengthening agents.
A refractory HEA matrix provides high hardness and wear resistance under extreme contact conditions.
A graded interface in a laser-clad coating minimizes residual stresses and preserves substrate properties.
The combination of HEA matrix and carbide reinforcement yields at least a 1.5-fold increase in microhardness and significantly lower wear rate and friction coefficient compared to untreated TC4.
